title: Potential effects of COVID-19 school closures on foundational skills and Country responses for mitigating learning loss
abstract: This article examines how school disruption and dropout relate to children’s foundational skills before and during the COVID-19 pandemic. Household survey data from 13 low- and lower-middle-income countries show that children who miss school or leave school tend to have weaker reading and numeracy outcomes. The authors also assess countries’ pandemic remote-learning responses and find that these efforts often did not reach every child, prevent dropout, or offset expected learning losses, particularly for marginalized children and those at pre-primary level.
